speaker: Doctor
text: I see you are presenting with fatigue, lower leg swelling, and weight loss. To help narrow this down, how long have these symptoms been occurring, and have you noticed any changes in your urine output or appetite?

speaker: Patient
text: 66-year-old white male. The patient reports a 10-day history of fatigue and bilateral lower leg swelling. He mentions a weight loss of 3.6 kg (8 lbs) over the past 6 months without trying. He has a history of chronic bronchitis and uses an albuterol inhaler as needed.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Have you experienced any shortness of breath, fever, or changes in your urine output recently? Also, do you have any history of heart failure or kidney disease?

REQUEST TEST: CBC, CMP, BNP, Urinalysis.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Hemoglobin: 11.2 g/dL, Leukocyte_count: 8500/mm3, Platelet_count: 130,000/mm3, Serum_Urea_nitrogen: 23 mg/dL, Glucose: 77 mg/dL, Creatinine: 1.6 mg/dL, Albumin: 1.8 mg/dL, Total_cholesterol: 475 mg/dL, Urine_Blood: Negative, Urine_Glucose: Negative, Urine_Protein: 4+, Urine_WBC: 0–1/hpf, Urine_Fatty_casts: Numerous, BNP: Not Provided, CBC: Not Provided, CMP: Not Provided, Urinalysis: Not Provided.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The results show significant proteinuria and fatty casts with severe hypoalbuminemia and hyperlipidemia, which strongly suggests nephrotic syndrome. Given your age and the 10-day onset of swelling, have you noticed any frothy urine, and do you have any history of diabetes or high blood pressure?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Nephrotic Syndrome (likely Membranous Nephropathy given age and presentation)
